output.summary: A perennial herb native to the southeastern United States, Carolina horsenettle has prickly stems and leaf veins and spreads through seeds and underground stems. Its berries resemble tomatoes, but all parts contain toxins in varying degrees and can cause illness when eaten.
output.edibilityNote: All parts contain toxins in varying degrees; eating them can cause illness, while the tomato-like fruit can cause severe effects or death.
